front_matter.title: Light-ray recurrence test: with additive bosons, scalars and graviton set the verdict

extraction.note: Adversarial attack on the open question of op.counted-mode-energy "which fields form the light-ray sea" and, through it, on the generation number of op.qft-structural-inputs. The recorded argument (prose in the problem's known field) is that a one-window recurrence of fermion parity with the zeta ordering needs the sea's light-ray central charge c to be a multiple of 24, that the spin-1/2 content alone gives 16 n_g, and that adding the integer-weight fields gives 78 at n_g = 3. This result takes the test as given and asks what its verdict on n_g depends on, under two readings of the bosons. (1) The additive reading: the null data of the gauge vectors, the scalar doublets and (eps = 1) the graviton are counted as real arrays of their own, on top of the sixteen Weyl arrays per generation. This reading is outside the CAR scope of (N+) and of the window reading, and it is not the reading of the stored postulate J3 (hawking.joint-j3-s-wave-reduction, in the past cone through the null-ordering result and the collapse result), which identifies each channel of every four-dimensional massless field, the graviton included, with the current boson of the s-wave theory, the bosonised current of the arrays. Under it: each field's null data are counted for every mass matrix and potential (the scalar case is new here; the fermion and abelian vector cases are stored; the non-abelian vector count and the integer weight of scalar data are argued); the twelve gauge vectors contribute 24 and drop out; the verdict tracks the doublets (n_g = 0 mod 3 needs n_h = 0 mod 6 for one window, 0 mod 3 for two; the two doublets of the linear rung field pass n_g = 1, 4 and fail 3; one doublet passes n_g = 2 under the two-window test); and a graviton counted additively, as J3's species list would have it, makes every content fail. (2) J3's reading: the integer-weight channels are currents of the arrays and add nothing, c = 16 n_g, and both tests give 3 | n_g. Either way the title's condition matters: the scalar and graviton content set the verdict only under the additive reading. On 9 November J3 was restated (version 2): its channel-reduction clause is assumed for spin 2 only, since synthesis.horizon-channels-of-scalar-dirac-and-maxwell-fields-are-two-dimensional derives it for spins 0, 1/2 and 1, while its current-boson identification is kept for every massless field; so under J3 version 2 the vectors and scalars are still read as currents of the arrays, and reading (2) is unchanged. J3 version 3 (same day) keeps the channel-reduction clause for even-parity spin 2 only, words the reduction per partial-wave channel, l >= |s|, and records that the identification is not one array tower per helicity channel; reading (2), in which the integer-weight channels add no array, is again unchanged, and is the reading J3 version 3 states. The modulus 3 appears because 16 is 2^4 and 24 = 8 * 3: any per-generation count of 8 or 16 mod 24 gives it. Under boson-fermion balance, the vanishing of the stored quartic Sakharov coefficient, c = 48 n_g and the test is blind to n_g. The two-window test (the evolution over two windows equal to 1, equivalently the one-window evolution equal to the grading up to sign) is included because it is the weakest operator-level recurrence; the one-window form adds one sign, the grading being normalised to +1 on the sea. The unit: on the arrays of (Q) the phase is written with the boundary-mode unit J (the boundary-mode algebra keeps its own complex unit, whose modes anticommute with I_4); on the continuum light ray it is I_4; the condition on c is the same. See synthesis.one-window-parity-recurrence-of-the-light-ray-sea-needs-twenty-four-arrays, whose clause (iv) derives the -kappa/24 of a real integer-weight component and whose one-window theorem is the form U = e^{2 pi J c/24} P assumed here; the zeta value used here is re-derived in the proof. The fifteen-component case of (iv) repeats that result's count as one instance of the general rule. What is not claimed: which fields form the sea, and anything fixing three rather than six or nine. Argued, not part of the statement: under spontaneous breaking the null-data count is unchanged (three Goldstone components become three longitudinal data, 2 * 9 + 3 * 3 + 1 = 28 = 24 + 4); and the recurrence cannot be posed on the whole Hamiltonian of a hole, whose label constant M gives the window phase L M = 8 pi M^2 = A/2 = 2S, so recurrence would put S in pi(Z + c/24), against S = (ln 2)/2 per array of (Q) version 3, since ln 2/pi is irrational (Gelfond: e^pi is transcendental; cited from memory). Prior art (literature, not premises; web-verified on 9 November 2026 unless marked): J. Wang, arXiv:2312.14928 (2023), the framing anomaly c_- = 0 mod 24 with c_- = 8 per family of 16 Weyl fermions read as Majorana-Weyl fermions on a domain wall: the conclusion 3 | n_g is prior art (Wang's arithmetic is 8 n_g = 0 mod 24, c = 1/2 per Weyl fermion, not 1 per complex array; the fifteen-component cases differ); I. Garcia-Etxebarria and M. Montero, JHEP 08 (2019) 003, arXiv:1808.00009, the Z16 Dai-Freed anomaly and sixteen per generation, and, in the same paper, a mod-9 Dai-Freed anomaly of baryon triality that cancels only when the number of generations is a multiple of 3, direct prior art for 3 | n_g; Z. Wan, J. Wang and S.-T. Yau, arXiv:2605.26202 (2026; abstract read), which cancels the mixed (B+L)-gauge-gravitational anomaly of a Standard Model without right-handed neutrinos by a Z_3 gauge TQFT, with N = N_c = N_f = 3 the minimal solution; E. Witten, Commun. Math. Phys. 121 (1989) 351 (framing anomaly, cited from memory). There c_- is the net chiral central charge, blind to bosons and to vector-like pairs; the additive light-ray count counts every field's null data with the same sign, so it agrees with theirs on fermion-only content (clause (iv)) and differs as soon as bosons or vector-like fermions enter. Transport-absent: two-dimensional central-charge bookkeeping on the series' recorded content.

levels.formal:
Units $\hbar = c = 1$. On a generator of a horizon in the scope of Premise (N$_{+}$), a \emph{complex array} is an array of Premise \claimref{singularity.q-joint-quasi-freeness-s-wave} version 3, weights $\kappa(k + \tfrac12)$, and a \emph{real array} the modes of one real chiral boson at integer weights $\kappa k$, which carries $-\kappa/24$ over a window $2\pi/\kappa$ in the zeta-regularised symmetric ordering ($\tfrac{\kappa}{2}\zeta(-1) = -\kappa/24$, as each complex array does, Theorem \claimref{synthesis.null-ordering-of-counted-units-is-zeta-symmetric}(ii)). For a content with $f$ complex and $b$ real arrays per generator put $c = f + b$, and call the \emph{one-window test} the condition $24 \mid c$ and the \emph{two-window test} the condition $12 \mid c$. They are the conditions for $e^{2\pi Jc/24} = 1$ and $e^{2\pi Jc/12} = 1$ ($J$ the unit of the boundary-mode arrays; on the continuum light ray the unit is $I_{4}$ and the conditions are the same), that is, for a window evolution of the form $e^{2\pi Jc/24}P$, with $P$ the grading normalised to $+1$ on the sea, to be $P$, respectively to be $\pm P$, equivalently the evolution over two windows to be $1$. That form is the reading under which the tests are posed; nothing below uses it. Call the \emph{additive reading} the reading in which the light-ray sea contains, besides the sixteen Weyl arrays per generation and in addition to them, one real array per real component of the null data of the gauge vectors, of the scalar doublets and, if $\epsilon = 1$, of the graviton. It lies outside the CAR scope of (N$_{+}$) and of the window reading, and it is not the reading of Premise \claimref{hawking.joint-j3-s-wave-reduction} (J3), which identifies every channel of each four-dimensional massless field with the current boson of the s-wave theory, a current of the arrays. Then:
\begin{enumerate}
\item[(i)] \emph{(Null data of each field, under the additive reading.)} On a null plane $N_{k}$ of $\Cl(1,3)$, $k = \gamma_{0} + \gamma_{3}$, $m = \gamma_{0} - \gamma_{3}$, $Q(k) = Q(m) = 0$, $\ip{k}{m} = 2$: every Weyl component gives one complex array for every mass matrix (Theorem \claimref{synthesis.slot-module-light-ray-arrays-are-weyl-components}(i)); every abelian gauge vector gives two real fields per generator (Theorem \claimref{synthesis.null-plane-photon-data-and-the-pair-currents-of-the-generators}(ii)), at integer boost weight (Theorem \claimref{synthesis.light-ray-good-part-of-a-spinor-is-two-chirality-arrays}(vi)), and the same count for each component of a non-abelian vector is argued, not proved; and every real scalar component gives one real field per generator for every potential $V$: for linearised solutions $\phi_{1}, \phi_{2}$ of $\nabla^{2}\phi + V'(\phi) = 0$ the current $\omega = \phi_{1}\nabla\phi_{2} - \phi_{2}\nabla\phi_{1}$ has $\nabla\cdot\omega = \phi_{1}\nabla^{2}\phi_{2} - \phi_{2}\nabla^{2}\phi_{1} = 0$, its flux through $N_{k}$ is $k\cdot\omega = \phi_{1}(k\cdot\nabla)\phi_{2} - \phi_{2}(k\cdot\nabla)\phi_{1}$, which contains neither $V$ nor a transverse derivative, and $\nabla^{2} = (k\cdot\nabla)(m\cdot\nabla) - \partial_{1}^{2} - \partial_{2}^{2}$, so the field equation fixes $(m\cdot\nabla)\phi$ on $N_{k}$ from $\phi$ there and one boundary value per generator (that these data carry integer weight, so form a real array, is argued). Hence, under the additive reading, a content of $n_{g}$ generations of the slot module (sixteen Weyl components each, Theorem \claimref{synthesis.slot-module-light-ray-arrays-are-weyl-components}(ii)), $n_{V}$ gauge vectors, $n_{s}$ real scalar components and, if a graviton's two helicities are counted, $\epsilon = 1$ ($\epsilon = 0$ otherwise) has
\[
c = 16n_{g} + 2n_{V} + n_{s} + 2\epsilon ,
\]
for every mass matrix and every scalar potential.
\item[(ii)] \emph{(The gauge vectors drop out, additive reading.)} With the connection-forced algebra $\su(3) \oplus \su(2) \oplus \uu(1)$ (Theorem \claimref{standard-model.connection-forced}), $n_{V} = 12$ and the vectors contribute $24$, so they change neither test. A gauge algebra of dimension $d$ drops out of the one-window test if and only if $12 \mid d$, and of the two-window test if and only if $6 \mid d$.
\item[(iii)] \emph{(The verdict on generations, additive reading.)} With $n_{V} = 12$ and $n_{s} = 4n_{h}$ ($n_{h}$ doublets), the one-window test holds if and only if $\epsilon = 0$ and $n_{h} \equiv 2n_{g} \pmod 6$, and the two-window test if and only if $\epsilon = 0$ and $n_{g} + n_{h} \equiv 0 \pmod 3$. So: with no scalar counted both hold exactly when $3 \mid n_{g}$; with one doublet the one-window test fails for every $n_{g}$ and the two-window test holds exactly when $n_{g} \equiv 2 \pmod 3$ ($c = 60$ at $n_{g} = 2$, where the window evolution is $-P$); with the eight real components of the linear rung field (Theorem \claimref{synthesis.linear-rung-field-has-a-neutral-normal-pair-in-the-scalon-sum}), $n_{h} = 2$, both hold exactly when $n_{g} \equiv 1 \pmod 3$, so $n_{g} = 1$ and $4$ pass and $n_{g} = 3$ fails ($c = 80$); with $\epsilon = 1$ (the graviton counted additively, as J3's species, every massless field, would include it) neither holds for any $n_{g}$, $n_{h}$ ($c \equiv 2 \pmod 4$). The content $n_{h} = 1$, $\epsilon = 1$ gives $c = 78$ at $n_{g} = 3$.
\item[(iv)] \emph{(The per-generation count.)} With $f$ Weyl components per generation and nothing else, the one-window test holds if and only if $24/\gcd(24, f)$ divides $n_{g}$ (the two-window test likewise with $12$), and the one-window modulus is $3$ exactly when $f \equiv 8$ or $16 \pmod{24}$. Fifteen components per generation (no neutral singlet, not a CPT halving of the slot module) give $8 \mid n_{g}$ and $4 \mid n_{g}$; sixteen components and the count of eight Majorana-Weyl units per generation give the same modulus $3$.
\item[(v)] \emph{(Boson-fermion balance, additive reading.)} If $b = 2f$, the balance of on-shell degrees of freedom at which the quartic coefficient $2N_{V} + N_{S} - 2N_{W}$ of the attachment's Sakharov sum vanishes (Theorem \claimref{synthesis.attachment-modules-give-sakharov-weights-cancelling-at-three-separate-generations}(iv), here with $\epsilon = 0$), then $c = 3f = 48n_{g}$ and both tests hold for every $n_{g}$; at $n_{g} = 3$, $N_{V} = 12$ this is that theorem's $N_{S} = 72$, with $c = 144$.
\item[(vi)] \emph{(J3's reading.)} If the integer-weight channels are read as J3 reads them, currents of the arrays, they add no array, $c = 16n_{g}$, and both tests hold exactly when $3 \mid n_{g}$.
\end{enumerate}
So the scalar and graviton content set the verdict only under the additive reading: there the tests single out $n_{g} \equiv 0 \pmod 3$ only with no graviton and a number of doublets divisible by $6$ (one window) or $3$ (two windows), and with the graviton counted no content passes; under J3's reading the verdict is $3 \mid n_{g}$. Which reading holds, and so which fields form the sea, is not decided here, and neither test distinguishes three generations from six or nine.
levels.technical: The recorded recurrence test asks that the evolution of the light-ray sea over one window of Killing time be exactly the fermion grading, which needs the light-ray central charge $c$ to be a multiple of $24$; the weaker requirement, the grading up to sign or two windows giving the identity, needs a multiple of $12$. This result reads off both verdicts under two readings of the bosons. In the additive reading the null data of the vectors, the scalars and possibly the graviton are counted as real arrays of their own on top of the sixteen Weyl arrays per generation; this reading lies outside the CAR scope of (N$_{+}$) and of the window reading and is not that of the stored channel postulate J3, which reads every massless field's channels as currents of the arrays. Null data are mass-blind: a Weyl component gives one complex array for every mass matrix and an abelian vector two real fields (both stored), and a real scalar one real field for every potential, since the symplectic flux through the null plane is $\phi_{1}(k\cdot\nabla)\phi_{2} - \phi_{2}(k\cdot\nabla)\phi_{1}$ and the potential enters only the constraint; the non-abelian vector count and the integer weight of scalar data are argued. So $c = 16n_{g} + 2n_{V} + n_{s} + 2\epsilon$. The twelve gauge vectors give exactly $24$ and drop out; the recorded failure at $78$ comes from the doublet's $4$ and the graviton's $2$. With $n_{h}$ doublets, one window needs $n_{h} \equiv 2n_{g} \pmod 6$ and two windows $n_{g} + n_{h} \equiv 0 \pmod 3$; a graviton, which J3's species list includes, makes both fail always. On the two doublets of the store's linear rung field the test passes at one and four generations and fails at three; with one doublet the two-window test passes at two. At the boson-fermion balance where the stored quartic Sakharov coefficient vanishes, $c = 48n_{g}$ and the test does not see $n_{g}$. Under J3's own reading the bosons add nothing, $c = 16n_{g}$, and both tests give $3 \mid n_{g}$; the modulus $3$ comes from $24 = 8 \cdot 3$ against the power of two $16$, and the Majorana-Weyl count $8$ of the literature gives the same.
levels.lay: An earlier argument suggested that a timing condition on the sea of particles running along a black hole's horizon (after one cycle the sea should return to itself exactly, up to the sign that distinguishes fermions) would require the number of particle generations to be a multiple of three, provided only the matter particles form that sea. Whether the force carriers, the Higgs field and the graviton add to that sea depends on a reading the series has not settled: its own rule for these fields treats them as built from the matter sea, in which case they add nothing and the multiple-of-three answer stands. If instead they are counted as extra members of the sea, the force carriers add exactly a harmless amount, while the Higgs field and a graviton shift the answer: with one Higgs doublet the strict condition can never be met and a slightly weaker form picks two generations; with the series' two Higgs doublets it picks one or four and rules out three; with a graviton it can never be met. In no reading can the condition tell three generations from six.
levels.one-liner: For the one-window ($24 \mid c$) and two-window ($12 \mid c$) recurrence tests of the light-ray sea: if the null data of vectors, scalars and ($\epsilon = 1$) the graviton are counted additively, as real arrays beside the sixteen Weyl arrays per generation (a reading outside (N$_{+}$), the window reading and J3), then $c = 16n_{g} + 2n_{V} + n_{s} + 2\epsilon$, the twelve vectors drop out, the verdict is $n_{h} \equiv 2n_{g} \pmod 6$, resp. $n_{g} + n_{h} \equiv 0 \pmod 3$, and never with a graviton; under J3's reading, bosons as currents of the arrays, $c = 16n_{g}$ and the verdict is $3 \mid n_{g}$.

proofs.main:
\emph{The tests.} Let $J$ be the unit of the boundary-mode arrays, $J^{2} = -1$, central among the modes (on the continuum light ray the unit is $I_{4}$, and everything below holds with $I_{4}$ for $J$). For $c \in \Z$, $e^{2\pi Jc/24} = \cos	frac{2\pi c}{24} + J\sin	frac{2\pi c}{24} = 1$ exactly when $c/24 \in \Z$; likewise $e^{2\pi Jc/12} = (e^{2\pi Jc/24})^{2} = 1$ exactly when $12 \mid c$, and $e^{2\pi Jc/24} = \pm1$ exactly when $12 \mid c$. An operator implementing the grading is fixed only up to sign; normalising it by $P = +1$ on the sea, the one-window test says that $e^{2\pi Jc/24}P$ is $P$, the two-window test that it is $\pm P$, equivalently that its square, the evolution over two windows, is $1$ ($P^{2} = 1$, $P$ commuting with the central unit). The form $e^{2\pi Jc/24}P$ is the reading under which the tests are posed: each complex array carries $-\kappa/24$ over a window $2\pi/\kappa$ in the null ordering (Theorem \claimref{synthesis.null-ordering-of-counted-units-is-zeta-symmetric}(i), (ii)), and a real array at integer weights carries, in the zeta-regularised symmetric ordering, $	frac12\sum_{n \ge 1}\kappa n = 	frac{\kappa}{2}\zeta(-1) = -\kappa/24$ (the zero mode carrying nothing), with excitation energies in $\kappa\Z$, so its one-window phase on excitations is $1$. \emph{Computed:} the finite part at $\varepsilon = 0$ of $\sum_{n \ge 0}(n + a)e^{-\varepsilon(n + a)}$ is $-	frac12B_{2}(a)$, by exact series inversion, so $\zeta(-1) = -	frac12B_{2}(1) = -	frac1{12}$ and a real array carries $-\kappa/24$; a real array at the half offset would carry $	frac{\kappa}{2}\zeta(-1, 	frac12) = +\kappa/48$, not the null-ordered window value. That the boson's zero point equals the null-ordered window value of the continuum, as Theorem \claimref{synthesis.null-ordering-of-counted-units-is-zeta-symmetric} shows for the CAR arrays, is part of the additive reading, not derived. None of this is used in (i) to (vi), which are statements about $c$.

\emph{The two readings.} Premise \claimref{hawking.joint-j3-s-wave-reduction} (J3), in the past cone of the null-ordering result, identifies each $(\omega, \ell, m, s)$ channel of every four-dimensional massless field with the current boson of the s-wave theory, which is a current of the arrays; read so, the integer-weight channels add no array and only the CAR count enters $c$. The additive reading instead counts their null data as further real arrays. Premise (N$_{+}$) and the window reading (\claimref{synthesis.window-reading-array-killing-energy}) are stated for CAR arrays (the arrays of Premise \claimref{singularity.q-joint-quasi-freeness-s-wave} version 3), so neither places vector, scalar or graviton data in the sea; the additive reading is an extension of both. Clauses (i) to (v) are statements under the additive reading and (vi) under J3's.

(i) \emph{Fermions and vectors} are the cited clauses: Theorem \claimref{synthesis.slot-module-light-ray-arrays-are-weyl-components}(i) shows that every Lorentz-covariant mass term, Dirac or Majorana, acts from the right and enters only the equation fixing $\Lambda(k)\psi$ from the free data $\Lambda(m)\psi$, one complex channel per Weyl component; Theorem \claimref{synthesis.null-plane-photon-data-and-the-pair-currents-of-the-generators}(ii) shows that the flux of the Maxwell symplectic current through $N_{k}$ in the gauge $k\cdot A = 0$ contains the two transverse components alone, so an abelian gauge vector gives two real fields on each generator. \emph{Argued, not proved:} for the factors of a non-abelian algebra the count is that of the free field, component by component in the adjoint, the interaction entering, as the mass terms do for the spinor, only through the equations off the plane (light-front gauge); no stored clause covers it. Both carry integer or half-integer boost weight as recorded in Theorem \claimref{synthesis.light-ray-good-part-of-a-spinor-is-two-chirality-arrays}(ii), (vi): spinor data weight $	frac12$ (the complex arrays), vector and bivector data integer weight (the real arrays); clause (vi) of that theorem does not cover scalars.

(iii) With $n_{V} = 12$, $n_{s} = 4n_{h}$: $c = 16n_{g} + 24 + 4n_{h} + 2\epsilon$. If $\epsilon = 1$, $16n_{g} + 24 + 4n_{h}$ is divisible by $4$, so $c \equiv 2 \pmod 4$ and $c$ is divisible neither by $12$ nor by $24$. If $\epsilon = 0$: $24 \mid 16n_{g} + 4n_{h}$ if and only if $6 \mid 4n_{g} + n_{h}$, that is $n_{h} \equiv -4n_{g} \equiv 2n_{g} \pmod 6$; and $12 \mid 16n_{g} + 4n_{h}$ if and only if $3 \mid 4n_{g} + n_{h}$, that is $n_{g} + n_{h} \equiv 0 \pmod 3$. The cases: $n_{h} = 0$ gives $3 \mid n_{g}$ in both; $n_{h} = 1$ is odd while $2n_{g}$ is even, so the one-window test never holds, and $n_{g} \equiv 2 \pmod 3$ for the other; $n_{h} = 2$ gives $2 \equiv 2n_{g} \pmod 6$, i.e. $n_{g} \equiv 1 \pmod 3$, and $n_{g} + 2 \equiv 0 \pmod 3$, the same.
